### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **169** documentable anchor(s).

**71** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `packageId (4 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **26** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a19d25a78cb29077ce587c341c7324ad8831a725` — the merge of head `2e1b12c26984e3e46d6f15f4370206d7e05f64a1` into base `41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a19d25a78cb29077ce587c341c7324ad8831a725 && git checkout a19d25a78cb29077ce587c341c7324ad8831a725
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb 2e1b12c26984e3e46d6f15f4370206d7e05f64a1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb && git merge --no-ff 2e1b12c26984e3e46d6f15f4370206d7e05f64a1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Check-runs on the head (read once).** 32 success, 13 skipped, 5 failure, 0 pending. Red: `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (8/8)`, `Test Core` (aggregate), `Type Check · consumer gates`, `TypeScript Type Check` (aggregate). Causes are M1 and M2 below.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The floor at save and at enforcement — right, with one wrinkle (S4).** Save: every `access_policy` key gets a write predicate (`organization-access-policy-binding.ts`, `accessPolicyWritePredicate`) that reads the floor per write from `manager.getDeploymentAccessFloor()` (the `auth` values as the settings pass applied them, env override included) and refuses a range outside every deployment range, a positive limit above the deployment's, a level below the deployment's; the settings service asks it from `setMany` only, which every settings door shares (`set` delegates). Enforcement: `effectiveSessionLimits` takes the smaller positive limit, `effectiveMfaLevel` the stronger level, and the organization list is judged in addition to the deployment list, which keeps its own auth-door gate. Write paths tried: settings API and bulk import both pass `setMany` (predicates run); a direct `sys_setting` row write and the boot migration bypass the predicates, but a looser stored value is not honoured — `readOrganizationAccessPolicy` reads an off-type value as the key's zero value and the combining rules hold the floor whatever is stored; a platform administrator writing on behalf passes the same predicates (the floor is not a per-caller rule). The deployment tightening later is in force at once with no stored row rewritten. One effect worth stating: an organization row that is now above a later-tightened floor still reads back on its settings page as the saved value while a different value is in force.
2. **`administrators` = ADR-0090 D12 exactly, no new concept — right.** `isMfaAdministrator` asks `resolveUserAuthzGrants` with the session's organization as `tenantId`: `PLATFORM_ADMIN` (kind 1), `TENANT_ADMIN` (kind 2 — `ORGANIZATION_ADMIN_GRANTS` names both `organization_admin` and `organization_admin_no_bypass`, so the wall-less ADR-0105 D4 variant is held too), and kind 3 through plugin-security's own `resolvePermissionSetsForContext` reading an `adminScope` with a `businessUnit`. Judged in the scoped organization, so an administrator of one organization is a member in another; a failing delegated check holds rather than lapses. Right.
3. **Sign-in judged by the floor only; scoping refused with 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED and no session row — right.** The deployment gate ahead of better-auth is unchanged; `refuseUnadmittedScoping` runs in `session.create.before` after ADR-0093 D9 picked the organization and in `session.update.before` when `activeOrganizationId` changes, throws `APIError('FORBIDDEN', { code: 'IP_NOT_ALLOWED' })` before the row is written, and only on a request that came through the HTTP door (the address `readRequestClientAddress()` holds is the one the deployment gate judged). `ipMatchesRange` reads IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4 and refuses an undetermined address while a list is set, the deployment gate's reading. What it does not do is judge a roaming session again (S3).
4. **Break-glass by the deployment list only — right as a rule, disclosed.** `judgeSessionScopingAddress` admits a user `isPlatformAdminUserId` answers true for (`hasPlatformAdminStanding`: the anchoring grant on a non-walled posture, the deployment-config list on every posture — so under objectos-ee's walled postures it is the config-named administrators, the platform's own standing rule). Disclosed in the manifest description ("Platform administrators are held to the deployment's ranges only"), the PR body and the changeset. It is the right break-glass: the organization's own administrators are held by the list they wrote, and the reopening hand is one the list never holds.
5. **Per-organization self-lock-out and the last-admin guard — holds; one wrinkle.** `allowedIpRangesWritePredicate(() => manager, { recovery: false })` judges the organization list against the saving request's address through the declared forwarded headers (same `resolveClientAddress` rule), without the env-override recovery sentence that reopens only the deployment list. `last-admin-guard.ts` (#5892) is untouched by the diff and keeps its per-organization reading. Wrinkle S4: the save check also holds a tenant-level administrator saving on an organization's behalf, whom the list never holds at enforcement.
6. **Both migrations converge and are idempotent; a partial failure is safe — right (by reading).** Toggle to level: skipped for `env`/`default` sources, a level reads `legacy: false` on the second boot. Column to row: the `auth.mfa_required` enrollment predicate is registered before the move and judges a stored legacy `true` as already-on, so the rewrite is not a turn-on; the `access_policy` predicates are registered after `migrateLegacyOrganizationRequireMfa`, so a stored `require_mfa` row moves even where two-factor is off; the set lands before the column clear, a failed set leaves the column (`error`, retried next boot), a failed clear finds `alreadySet` next boot and only clears; the `limit: 5000` page converges over boots. The column clear under `SYSTEM_CTX` passes the engine's static readonly strip, which runs on `!context.isSystem` only, and the ADR-0092 D2 guard, which clamps user-context writes only — read in `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, not pinned: the move's test drives an engine double, not a real engine with the now-`readonly` column.
7. **The narrowing is stated honestly — mostly (S5, S8).** PR body and changeset name all three: the `auth.mfa_required` value shape, the read-only column, the renamed option, with the FROM → TO mapping and the ADR-0087 marker. Not said: a *write* of `true`/`false` to `auth.mfa_required` is now refused at the settings door by the select's option table (S5), and a JS host still passing `mfaRequired: true` is silently unheld (S8).

### ② Semver level

Changesets: `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, `@objectstack/platform-objects` each `patch`, with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, a BREAKING banner, the migration and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required`, runtime-interface-only). Against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist 3: the level follows the kind alone and a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` with its banner — so `patch` is right **if** `none` is right. `none` is right: the diff touches no `packages/spec` path; the `access_policy` manifest is a runtime registration of a built-in `SettingsManifest` instance and its values are `sys_setting` data, not a key, value or type a metadata author writes; `readonly: true` on `sys_organization.require_mfa` changes what a *data* writer may write to a platform-owned column (ADR-0092 D2's own tier), not what a metadata author can author; the renamed `AuthManagerOptions` field is a runtime option. CI's `Check Changeset`, `check:adr-0087-registration` and the docs guards are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) cloud `settings-cross-org-doors.test.ts` — disclosed in the wrong place; S5.** On cloud `main` (`b59b27484f`, pinned to objectstack `c50e0dfa`) the test writes `settings.set('auth', 'mfa_required', true, {})` at `:533` and expects `true` back at `:552`. After the pin moves past this head, `setMany`'s option-table validation refuses `true` (`invalid_option`). The PR body and the changeset do not say so; the changeset's upgrade note ("saved as on now reads `everyone`") is true of a stored value and silent about a refused write. The disclosure exists only in the card's report comment. Add the sentence to the changeset and name the consumer in the PR body.
- **(b) `organizationMfaNotices.ts` — inert; S6.** `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/organizationMfaNotices.ts`, `AppContent.tsx:969` and the `en.ts:2205` strings now fire for no write (the column is `readonly` and off the editable whitelist). Disclosed in the Acceptance notes, neither removed nor filed. Dead code over a retired column stays dead until someone files it: a `ui/` card, or the removal in this PR under Post-Task Checklist 4.
- **(c) the judged address — disclosed; S7.** An organization administrator learns `constraint.clientAddress` only from the refusal; `GET /admin/client-address` stays platform-admin only. Not a lock-out risk (the save that leaves the address out is refused), a usability gap. A follow-up card for a `setup.write`-gated address read.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Concurrent sessions — counted per user, capped per organization: S1.** `enforceConcurrentCap` counts every live `sys_session` of the user, whatever organization each is scoped to, and takes the cap of the organization the *new* session was scoped to. Two consequences: a sign-in to a strict organization evicts the user's sessions in other organizations; and the sweep runs only in the sign-in after-hook, so N sessions opened against a lax organization and then switched into a strict one (`session.update`) exceed the strict organization's cap, which is never swept. Decide the semantics (count sessions scoped to that organization, and sweep on a switch) and state it in the key's description.
- **A user in two organizations with different limits — by design, with one hole: S2.** Limits follow `session.activeOrganizationId` per request (`customSession`), so organization A's idle/absolute limits bind while the session works in A. The hole: the switch into A is judged for A's IP list, not A's limits, and the switch itself refreshes `last_activity_at`, so a session that idled past A's idle limit while active in B is re-admitted to A's data. The absolute limit is caught on the next request in A; the idle limit is not. Judge the target organization's limits at the switch.
- **Switching organization to evade a stricter idle limit** — see S2; the evasion holds for idle, not for absolute.
- **IPv6 and proxies — right.** One address for every judgement: the one the door established by the `server.trustProxy` rule (leftmost `X-Forwarded-For`, then `X-Real-IP`, only when trusted; else the peer), read from the request state the deployment gate wrote. `parseIpRange`/`ipMatchesRange` compare by family, an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address as its IPv4 address, and `rangeWithin` refuses a cross-family containment; an undetermined address is refused while a list is set. The save door judges the same address through `FORWARDED_CLIENT_ADDRESS_HEADERS`.
- **Cache staleness — acceptable, worth stating.** Per-organization policy is cached `ORG_ACCESS_POLICY_TTL_MS` = 30 s and dropped by the `access_policy` change listener; the "any organization requires MFA" flag is reset on that change and otherwise refreshed every 60 s. The listener is in-process, so another node applies a changed policy up to 30 s (60 s for the flag) late — the same window the deployment's `auth` keys already have. Name it in the module header.
- **The roaming session — S3.** The organization list is judged where a session gains an organization and never again; the deployment list judges every auth-door request. A tightened organization list leaves sessions opened from now-excluded addresses live until they expire. Disclosed in the Acceptance notes; asymmetric with the deployment list and with the idle limit, which `customSession` does re-judge. Either judge the organization list in `customSession` too, or say in the key's description that it binds at sign-in and switch only.

**Findings.**
- **M1 (must-fix)** — `Test Core (1/8)` red on the head's own change: `packages/cli/test/connect-agent-both-halves-wire.pin.test.ts:273,297` pin the platform administrator's Setup tree at 31 entries; the new `nav_settings_access_policy` entry makes it 32 and the PR does not move the pin or its count comment.
- **M2 (must-fix)** — `Test Core (8/8)` and `Type Check · consumer gates` (`check:app-nav-i18n`: "nav_settings_access_policy … author's literal 'Access policy'") red on the merge: origin/main `a11ef71e93` (#30951) added `packages/platform-objects/src/apps/translations/zh-Hant.ts` and zh-Hant to `setup-nav-hub-parity.test.ts`'s locales after the merge-base; this PR ships the zh-Hant hub title `存取原則` in service-settings but no zh-Hant sidebar label. Merge `origin/main` and add the label.
- **S1 (should-fix)** — concurrent cap counted per user across organizations, chosen per organization, never swept on a switch (④).
- **S2 (should-fix)** — an active-organization switch is judged for the target's IP list but not its idle/absolute limits (④).
- **S3 (should-fix)** — the organization IP list binds at scoping only; a tightened list does not end roaming sessions (④).
- **S4 (should-fix)** — the per-organization self-lock-out save check holds a tenant-level administrator saving on behalf, whom the list never holds at enforcement (①.5).
- **S5 (should-fix)** — the refused `true` write to `auth.mfa_required` and the cloud consumer test are not named in the PR body or changeset (③a).
- **S6 (should-fix)** — `organizationMfaNotices.ts` left inert, neither removed nor filed (③b).
- **S7 (should-fix)** — no address read for an organization administrator before saving (③c).
- **S8 (should-fix)** — a retired `mfaRequired: true` option is dropped silently at runtime; refuse the retired key at `AuthManager` construction as `assertAllowedIpRanges` refuses a bad list, so a requirement never lapses unannounced (①.7).
